title: Largest Palindromic Number
summary: Given a string of digits, return the largest palindromic number possible by rearranging the digits, ensuring no leading zeros and using at least one digit.
statement: Given a string of digits, return the largest palindromic number possible by rearranging the digits, ensuring no leading zeros and using at least one digit.
constraints: Use at least one available digit to form the numerically largest palindrome with no leading zero.
Not every digit must be used; return the result as a string.
hints: The left half determines the palindrome’s length and most significant digits.
Take every available nonzero pair from nine downward, then zero pairs only after a nonzero leading pair exists.
Choose the largest remaining odd-count digit as the optional middle and mirror the left half.
More paired digits always increases length, and within a fixed length descending outer digits maximize the number lexicographically.
editorial: More paired digits always increases length, and within a fixed length descending outer digits maximize the number lexicographically.

tests.explanation: Use paired sevens and fours around the best remaining middle digit nine to form 7449447.
Zero cannot lead a multi-digit number, so the best palindrome is the single digit nine.
